macro.regime: Oil-driven inflation scare plus an AI-capex financing wobble trigger a risk-off, metals-liquidation day
macro.narrative: Thursday Oct 22 was a genuine risk-off session with two distinct, compounding drivers. First, a widening Houthi drone campaign against Saudi energy infrastructure (strikes near the Shaybah oilfield and King Fahd airport) pushed Brent up 3.66% to $112.80 and WTI up 1.89% to $98.99, reviving 'rates stay higher for longer' fears -- that oil-driven inflation scare is the best-sourced explanation for why gold and silver sold off HARD alongside equities rather than acting as a hedge (SLV -5.59%, GLD -2.63%, GDX -5.80%, SILJ -6.52%, PAAS -7.27%), with miners falling far harder than the metals as funds cut the most liquid, most extended longs first after silver's parabolic 2026 run. Second, and separately, Tesla's cut to 2026 capex guidance and Meta's AI-expansion-linked non-voting-share plan reignited AI-infrastructure-financing doubts (CoreWeave's reported ~$50B debt load, Goldman estimating a further $19.5-23B funding need), driving the VIX up 9.94% to 19.03 and the Nasdaq down 1.57% to 26,008.86 even as the Dow rose 0.71% and Russell 2000 rose 0.38% -- a narrow, mega-cap-AI-concentrated selloff rather than a broad one. Hong Kong tech fell further than this dashboard's automated price feed initially showed: the Hang Seng Index actually closed -3.03% at 22,934.68 (not the stale 23,867.74 carried in the feed), driven by a fresh Alibaba-specific shock -- China's SAMR summoned Alibaba, JD.com, PDD and ByteDance over counterfeit-goods/quality-standard violations in livestream commerce, on top of the standing Tencent/SMIC AI-chip-export-control overhang. The Fed remains priced to hold at the Oct 27-28 FOMC (~85-94% per Kalshi/Polymarket) but the residual tail has shifted toward a hike, not a cut, consistent with oil's inflationary pass-through. Net: this reads as two live, compounding risk events (Middle East energy-supply risk, AI-capex-financing doubts) rather than a single confirmed regime change, but the VIX spike and gold/silver's failure to hedge argue for a smaller risk budget into tonight's flash PMIs/UMich data and next week's FOMC.
